# SessionLockHeldDuringBlockingCall

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Detect a known blocking sleep/usleep or network operation while an active session with a known locking handler remains owned by the scope.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
ini_set('session.save_handler', 'files'); session_start(); sleep(8); session_write_close();
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Release the session lock before blocking when safe.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report a known blocking sleep/usleep or network operation while an active session with a known locking handler remains owned by the scope.
- Resolve builtin calls and named arguments before checking the contract. Project-local callees are considered only when their bodies or immutable summaries establish the required facts. The default is disabled; enable only when the stated intent matches the application.
- The session is active when the last session operation reaching the blocking call is a `session_start` that keeps the session open: it has no options, or its options are a literal array with constant string keys whose `read_and_close` entry is absent or known to be falsy.
- The handler is known to lock only when the last handler selection written before that `session_start` is an unconditional `ini_set`/`ini_alter` of `session.save_handler` to the literal `'files'`. Only writes in the same scope are considered.
- For flow-dependent conditions, require a reachable source-to-use path with no intervening invalidation. Unknown calls, ambiguous aliases, recursion or analysis-budget exhaustion cannot establish definite facts.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Nonlocking handlers, earlier successful session_write_close, required atomic session work and unknown handler configuration are excluded.
- `session_start` with `read_and_close` enabled, or with options that cannot be read statically (a non-literal value, a spread, an unpacked or non-string key, an unknown `read_and_close` value): the lock may already be released.
- After the `'files'` selection and before `session_start`: another or unknown value written to `session.save_handler`, an ini write whose option name is unknown, `ini_restore` of that option, `session_set_save_handler`, or `session_module_name` called with an argument, whether conditional or not. The handler in effect is then unknown.
- A handler selection written after `session_start` proves nothing about the session already open.
- Unresolved targets, incomplete required facts, suppressed findings and PHP versions lacking the referenced API or language feature produce no report. User declarations shadowing builtin names are not builtin contracts.

## Fix

No automatic fix: early close may discard later writes or break atomic session behavior.

## PHP versions

Apply only on PHP versions supporting the referenced APIs and syntax (within PHP 5.3–8.5). Builtin behavior and argument contracts follow the configured PHP version. Extension-specific calls require resolved extension API symbols; do not treat same-named application functions as extension calls.

## Options

None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "SessionLockHeldDuringBlockingCall": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore SessionLockHeldDuringBlockingCall
```
